doc.title: Karolina Strassmayer interviewed by Monk Rowe, May 25, 2023

chapter: Her music, free jazz and playing
title: Naming spontaneous pieces
summary: Titles are descriptive or reflect what is on her mind, as with Of Mystery and Beauty; the music itself is enough.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: What about song titles? I was looking at a couple — now it seemed to me that a couple of the song titles on your videos could be descriptive. There was “Mallets and Air” and you had a mallet player and you were playing the flute. Okay. Now I’m not sure if that was totally on purpose but I remember talking to one person, a New Orleans musician who called themself the last free jazz player — Kidd Jordan. And they were talking about song titles after they had done quote a free album. And one they named “Last of the Chicken Wings” because the chicken wings had all been eaten. And so how do you name things that are spontaneous?

Either by being descriptive like “Mallets and Air” definitely, sure, that’s — or another one on this recent CD is like “Drum Roll, Please.” And it started with a drum roll. But sometimes I call things, I call tunes for things that just go on in my life. You know for instance a few years ago I did this record “Of Mystery and Beauty” and that’s really when I began to think about what we were talking about before, this desire to create beauty. And that I see our jobs as musicians really to be in this mystery and beauty of creation. So this is really a bigger topic in my life then and it has nothing to do with the
song itself it just is something that I think about at that point in my life when I write that song. So that’s mostly how my tunes have titles.
We seem to go to great lengths to analyze things and give them meaning when perhaps the music itself is enough.

But that’s what we humans do, right? We want to give a bone to our mind, to always like categorize things or analyze things or name them. I guess it’s a very human thing but you’re right, the music is enough.
